correctness.rationale: The next excited mask is the threshold mask minus the current excited and refractory masks; the next refractory mask is exactly the current excited mask. Independently enumerated every excited mask and every refractory submask of its complement, for each graph, in eight disjoint chunks. After excitation first vanishes an initially nonzero trajectory needs exactly one additional refractory step. Reproduced all six cells on both graphs, including sharp maxima four and five, and reproduced the exact set of 1,088 Shrikhande codes. Independently enumerated all adjacency-preserving permutations by bijection backtracking (no assumption of affinity), obtaining 192, and recovered all eight specified representative-size pairs. The frozen weighted count is valid because each specified next-excited subset fixes the refractory bits exactly on the eligible mask and leaves all other nonexcited bits free; its two group totals were also recomputed. Literal scalar updates give witnesses 7546 → 93932 → 334827 → 354294 → 0 and 563061 → 2947984 → 22795283 → 38268153 → 54 → 0.
residual_risks: The frozen C++ programs were inspected, not executed; the independent Python reproduction covers the full finite finding. No claims about other thresholds or formal verification.

value.rationale: Sharp relaxation time and its spatial symmetry classes are natural exact invariants for the standard nonisomorphic strongly regular twins. Their common spectrum predicts identical qualitative extinction under the general obstruction, but not the observed four-versus-five separation. The full labelled distribution and maximal-shell classification are useful reproducible finite benchmarks beyond a witness of graph nonisomorphism.
residual_risks: The result measures one fixed nonlinear update and two graphs; no universality of the observed sharp cutoffs is implied.
